conclusion.root_cause: Product-api v2.4.0 deployment at 14:08:00Z introduced a dual-failure condition: (1) N+1 query pattern in the new availability join path executing per-item SELECT with LEFT JOIN averaging 220ms (vs baseline <50ms), holding database connections 4x longer and exhausting the reduced per-pod connection pool (20→8), and (2) miscalculated connection pool sizing that failed to account for product-db max_connections=100 hard limit. The replica scale-up from 3→9 pods created 72 base connections (9×8), which combined with checkout-api (~15), other services (~10), and maintenance connections (~5) totaled 102 connections, exceeding the database's 100-connection ceiling at 14:18Z. The inefficient N+1 queries saturated the smaller pools faster than connection cycling could recover, while the database connection limit created a hard ceiling that prevented any pod from acquiring additional connections, cascading 503 errors to checkout-api and triggering 5xx spike from 0.4% to 14.2%.

conclusion.remediation: IMMEDIATE: (1) Rollback product-api to v2.3.x to eliminate N+1 query pattern and restore baseline connection hold times (<50ms). (2) Increase product-db max_connections from 100 to 150+ to provide headroom for current topology (72 base + 30 overhead). SHORT-TERM: (3) Optimize availability join path in v2.4.0 to use batch queries instead of per-item SELECT (eliminate N+1 pattern). (4) Right-size product-api connection pool: either increase per-pod pool from 8 to 12-15 OR reduce replicas from 9 to 6 to stay within database connection budget. (5) Implement connection pool monitoring alerts: trigger at >80% pool utilization or wait time >100ms. LONG-TERM: (6) Establish capacity planning process that validates total connection count (pods × pool size + overhead) against database max_connections before any deployment. (7) Add database connection budget tracking to deployment pipelines. (8) Consider read replicas or connection pooling proxy (PgBouncer) to decouple application connection pools from database connection limits.
